subject: Social Media
title: Section 230
description: A quick, practical guide to Section 230.

hook.text: Twenty-six words written in 1996 created the modern internet. They shield platforms from liability for user content.

buildup.text: Section 230 says platforms aren't publishers. They host content without being responsible for it—unlike newspapers.

discovery.text: Without 230, every lawsuit over a user comment could bankrupt a startup. The law enabled social media to exist.

twist.text: Critics say it lets platforms profit from harm without consequence. Defenders say removing it would kill free speech.

climax.text: Both parties want to reform 230—for opposite reasons. The left wants more moderation. The right wants less.

punchline.text: The internet's shield is also its blindfold.

quiz.question: What does Section 230 protect platforms from?
